verdict.root_cause: At 13:57:09 platform-automation lowered the memory limit on frauddetection-service to 200m and, unlike the two earlier lowerings that day, did not revert it [tr_c79f3ed6b0c4]. Within ~17 seconds the service entered a restart loop: normal Kafka order-consumption logging stops at 13:57:08 and never resumes, and the JVM/OTel-agent startup banner repeats three times in quick succession and then roughly every 60 seconds through 14:04:23, including at 14:03:20 [tr_9bdc8983d0c5]. Every cycle ends silently with no throwable, shutdown message, or dependency error, which is the signature of the process being terminated externally before application logging is established rather than crashing in-process [tr_9bdc8983d0c5]. The mechanism that is failing right now is that the container cannot hold its working set inside the 200m ceiling and is killed for exceeding it, so the fraud consumer never reaches the point of processing a record; the 14:03 alert is mid-incident, not onset. The remedy is to restore the prior memory limit (and stop the automation loop that keeps re-applying it).
verdict.reasoning: Three independent legs converge. Changes: the only edits in the window are five resource_limits changes by platform-automation, with the last one lowering memory ~5 minutes before onset and left unreverted; no deploy, image, dependency or flag change exists to explain the failure [tr_c79f3ed6b0c4]. Logs: a repeating startup sequence with no application logging after 13:57:08 and no error output on any cycle, at a fixed ~60s cadence — a process being torn down and re-created, not one running slowly or hitting a poison-pill message or a failing dependency [tr_9bdc8983d0c5]. Traces: where fraud consumer spans exist (13:37-13:54) they complete in ~0.1ms with no errors, and checkout latency is dominated by the shippingservice→quoteservice hop, so frauddetectionservice was not slow or erroring before the limit change and is not the source of latency [tr_1b0076ceab28]. I classify this as resource_exhaustion rather than bad_config by the stated rule: the configuration edit is how it started, but what the service is doing wrong now is exceeding a memory ceiling and being killed for it. The fix that would stop it is nevertheless restoring the prior limit, hence config_revert. Confidence is held at medium because the confirming telemetry was never retrieved: both metric dispatches returned only an error-ratio series with zero samples in every window, so container working-set, memory-limit, restart-count and OOMKill series remain entirely unmeasured and the specialist explicitly refused to treat OOM as confirmed [tr_e6f3743d8265, tr_de605d2905f2].
open_questions: No container memory working-set, memory-limit, restart-count or OOMKilled/termination-reason data was ever retrieved, so the kill mechanism is inferred from log shape and timing rather than observed [tr_e6f3743d8265].

Whether the kills are OOM at the cgroup level or a liveness/startup-probe timeout caused by a memory-starved JVM starting too slowly — both fit silent ~60s-interval restarts, and pod events would separate them [tr_9bdc8983d0c5].

Why the two earlier lowerings the same day were reverted within 11-12 minutes and this one was not: whether the automation is expected to revert and failed, and whether it will re-lower the limit after a manual revert [tr_c79f3ed6b0c4].

The monotonic span-count decline (49→25) and the whole-async-leg loss at 13:55:47 — including the checkoutservice publish span, accounting consumer and emailservice call — is unexplained by a frauddetectionservice restart and begins before 13:57; it may be a separate collector/sampling issue [tr_1b0076ceab28].

Trace evidence stops at 13:55:47, so there is no trace coverage of the restart period at all, and error-ratio metrics are absent across all windows — the blast radius on checkout/order flow during 13:57-14:05 was never measured [tr_1b0076ceab28, tr_de605d2905f2].

The persistently degrading shippingservice→quoteservice hop was present before and during the window and was never investigated; it is unrelated to the fraud restarts but may be its own problem [tr_1b0076ceab28].

alternatives.root_cause: The 200m value is itself an unworkable setting — the JVM cannot complete startup within it at all — making the wrong value, not gradual exhaustion under load, the thing that breaks the service.
alternatives.why_not: Same edit, same remedy, but the taxonomy assigns a limit lowered until a process is killed for exceeding it to resource_exhaustion; distinguishing 'cannot start at all' from 'exceeds ceiling during startup' would need the memory and termination-reason series that were never returned [tr_e6f3743d8265].

alternatives.root_cause: A liveness/readiness probe kills the container on a fixed interval for reasons unrelated to memory, and the coincident limit change is incidental.
alternatives.why_not: No probe configuration change appears anywhere in the window — the only recorded edits are the five memory-limit changes — and the restart loop begins 17 seconds after the unreverted lowering, which a probe-only explanation leaves as coincidence [tr_c79f3ed6b0c4, tr_9bdc8983d0c5].

proposal.expected_effect: Restoring the configuration frauddetectionservice held before the 13:57:09 resource_limits edit (memory limit back off the 200m ceiling) should end the kill/restart cycle. Observable in Loki on {service="frauddetection-service"}: the JVM tool-options / OTel-agent startup banner should appear once after the recreate and then NOT recur at ~60s intervals, and the "Consumed record with orderId ... updated total count to: N" lines that stopped at 13:57:08 should resume and the count increment steadily. The two earlier lowerings that day were reverted and the service kept consuming, which is the precedent for this effect [tr_c79f3ed6b0c4].
proposal.if_wrong: Falsified if, after the recreate, startup banners keep repeating at roughly 60s spacing with no "Consumed record" line appearing within 4 minutes - that would mean the process is being killed for a reason other than the 200m ceiling (e.g. a liveness/startup-probe timeout, which fits the same silent ~60s pattern and was never separated from OOM because no container memory, restart-count or OOMKilled/termination-reason data was ever retrieved [tr_e6f3743d8265]). Also falsified in a different way if the loop stops but platform-automation writes another memory-limit lowering into change history shortly after: the same actor performed five such edits and the reason this one was not auto-reverted is unknown [tr_c79f3ed6b0c4], so the fix may be undone within minutes. Note the standard error-ratio metric for this service has no samples in any window [tr_de605d2905f2], so confirmation must come from logs, not metrics - do not expect a metric to move.
proposal.risk: If the kills are probe-timeout rather than cgroup-OOM, this changes nothing and costs a container recreate: one more restart on top of a service already restarting, and the in-flight Kafka consumer position/cache is discarded again. If the recorded "previous configuration" contains more than the memory limit (the change entries only describe resource_limits, so the full reverted payload is unverified), reverting could restore other stale values alongside it. The revert also does not stop the automation loop; treating the incident as closed after it could mask a re-lowering. Finally, the unexplained monotonic span loss and whole-async-leg drop starting 13:55:47 - before this change - is not addressed by this action and may be a separate collector/sampling fault [tr_1b0076ceab28]; if that is the real reporting problem, this revert will appear to fail for the wrong reason.
proposal.blast_radius: frauddetectionservice only - it is the sole service in this incident's blast radius. It is an async Kafka order consumer, so the recreate window has no synchronous caller to reset a connection; the effect on others is that fraud-check consumption of the orders topic pauses for the duration of the recreate and then begins draining whatever backlog accumulated since 13:57:08. Any dashboard or alert keyed on frauddetection-service restarts will see one further restart event at apply time before the count flattens. Trace coverage of the 13:57-14:05 period is absent entirely [tr_1b0076ceab28], so the downstream checkout/order impact both before and after this action is unmeasured - do not claim the order flow was restored, only that the consumer resumed.

triage_judgement.reasoning: A single critical alert on frauddetectionservice with no open incidents to attribute it to; critical severity is not dismissible without evidence.
